Methods

Stage 3 Concept ⏱ 16 min 📖 Glossary

A method is a reusable recipe card: name it once, cook it anywhere. Every repeated block you refuse to extract becomes copy-paste rot that must be fixed in five places.

🔎 Motivating questionWhy do restaurants print menus instead of explaining each dish table by table?

Objectives

  • Define and call a method
  • Explain reuse benefit
  • Read a call stack simply

Needs first: Nested Loops

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

The vending machine. Press B3 (call it), hidden machinery runs fixed steps, a snack drops (maybe with change = return value). You reuse the machine without knowing — or caring — about its insides.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: vending machines jam on bent coins. Methods jam on bad inputs — garbage in, garbage out. Methods reuse LOGIC, not judgment; validate inputs or document limits.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

Define once: static void greet() { ... }. Call often: greet(); — each call jumps in, runs the body, jumps back to the line after the call.

Calls make code DRY (Don’t Repeat Yourself): fix the card once, every caller improves. Copy-paste makes bugs immortal — the fix lands in 3 copies, the 4th keeps crashing.

void means “no takeaway value” — it DOES something (prints) but RETURNS nothing. Value-returning methods (next lesson) HAND something back.

Methods also NAME ideas: printBill() tells readers what 20 lines do. A well-named method is a comment that cannot rot.

⚙️ Tech details — precise facts
  • A method signature = name + parameter types. Return type is NOT part of it (you cannot overload by return alone).
  • Each call gets a fresh stack frame: its own parameters and locals, destroyed on return. Recursion is just frames piling up.
  • static here means “callable without an object” — main is static, so the methods it calls directly must be static too (until objects arrive in Stage 5).

3 Watch it move: Vending calls

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
public class Chef {
  static void greet() {
    System.out.println("Welcome!");
  }

  public static void main(String[] args) {
    greet();
    greet();
    System.out.println("Seated: 2 guests");
  }
}
▶ Output Welcome! Welcome! Seated: 2 guests
  • greet is defined ONCE as a recipe card.
  • Called twice — the body runs twice.
  • Change the card once, both servings improve.
▶️ Run it yourselfSave exactly as Main.java, then javac Main.java and java Main. Every full program in this course works this way.
💡 Why this output?Each call executes the body fully, returns to the line after the call, and continues. Two calls, two greetings.

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: Defining a method but never calling it.Why: The card sits in the drawer forever — zero effect, zero error, pure confusion.
✅ Fix: Call it from main (or from another called method).
❌ Mistake 2: Copy-pasting a 10-line block three times “for now”.Why: “For now” is forever: the tripled bug gets fixed twice and survives in copy three.
✅ Fix: Extract a method the SECOND time you paste.
❌ Mistake 3: Calling a non-static method from static main.Why: Instance methods need an object; main has none yet — “non-static method cannot be referenced” greets you.
✅ Fix: Add static (for now — Stage 5 explains the real story).

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Extract it

Two identical receipt-printing blocks sit in main. Extract them.

HintName it printBill(), call it twice.
Solutionstatic void printBill() { ...the block... } then printBill(); printBill();
Call counting

greet() is called 3 times and prints one line each. How many lines total?

HintEach call = one full run.
Solution3 lines.

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • Define once, call often.
  • Each call jumps in, runs, jumps back.
  • void = does things, returns nothing.
  • Name methods after the idea they package.
🧠 Recall challengeNarrate what happens, step by step, when main calls greet().
✏️ Do on your ownExtract one repeated block from your old code into a method.
